svg.title: Water when supplies are limited: source and equipment screen
svg.desc: Part one of a Victorian field-water sequence. Protect water already safe to drink and do not search if no more source is needed. Stay within the book's stay-or-move plan. For boiling, confirm a suitable unsealed heat-safe pot, a lawful heat source that can be operated exactly as instructed, a stable non-combustible cooling place and a clean cup or closable drinking-water container if serving or storing. No thermometer, transfer ladle, special dry rim or separate cup for every person is required. Reject salt or brackish water, algae or scum, floodwater, current warnings, sewage, mine, farm or industrial runoff, fuel, ash and firefighting chemicals. No identified warning does not prove safety. Collect only from stable ground without climbing or wading. Settling and cloth can remove grit but do not disinfect. No dependable zero-equipment treatment is supplied.
svg.text: Water when supplies are limited — 1 of 2
WARNING — NO METHOD MAKES EVERY SOURCE SAFE
Editorial confidence: 95% limits; 80% field handling.
These figures describe wording—not safety or treatment success.
Salt, algal toxins, chemicals and metals are rejected, not fixed.
1 PROTECT WATER ALREADY SAFE TO DRINK
Keep it in its intact clean container. Check lids and leaks.
Reduce avoidable effort and heat exposure while arranging help.
2 DO YOU ACTUALLY NEED ANOTHER SOURCE?
Do not search just because a blue map line or tank symbol exists.
NO — STOP SEARCHING
Protect water and stay in the rescue plan.
YES — CONTINUE CAUTIOUSLY
Stay inside Chapter 4's movement boundary.
3 IS THE SIMPLE BOILING SYSTEM READY?
• Suitable unsealed heat-safe cooking pot.
• Lawful heat source you can operate exactly as instructed.
• Stable non-combustible place where the pot can cool.
• Clean cup or clean closed storage if serving or storing.
No thermometer, transfer ladle or special dry-rim method is required.
The heat source must still pass every legal and fire-safety gate.
NO / UNKNOWN: THERE IS NO BOILING ROUTE
Use the emergency no-treatment branch. Do not improvise a vessel or fire.
4 IS ANY RED FLAG PRESENT OR REASONABLY SUSPECTED?
Salt or brackish water; algae or surface scum; floodwater;
a current warning; sewage; mine, farm or industrial runoff;
fuel, ash, firefighting foam or retardant; burnt-property runoff;
unusual odour, colour, dead fish or another contamination sign.
Normal appearance and taste cannot clear a warning or suspicion.
No identified red flag still leaves natural water suspect.
YES / UNSURE — REJECT
Reselect if that can be done safely.
Ordinary boiling will not fix this source.
NO FLAG FOUND
The source is still suspect.
Continue to safe collection and treatment.
5 COLLECT WITHOUT CREATING ANOTHER EMERGENCY
Use firm ground. Do not climb a steep bank or wade into water.
Use the pot directly if it can be filled safely, or a suitable
UNTREATED collector. Keep raw water away from clean openings.
6 MUDDY WATER: GRIT REMOVAL ONLY
If an extra untreated receiver is available, let mud settle.
Pour the clearer upper water through clean tightly woven cloth.
Settling and cloth remove some grit. They do not remove germs.
A homemade sand, gravel or charcoal filter is not treatment.
NEXT: ROLLING-BOIL TREATMENT — 2 OF 2
WORKING DRAFT — NOT FIELD-APPROVED
